materials.name: Yb0.35Co4Sb12
processing_method: melting
quenching
ball milling
hot pressing

processing_steps.notes: Pure elements of Co, Sb, and Yb were weighted according to the stoichiometric ratio of Yb x Co 4 Sb 12 (x = 0.2, 0.35, 0.45, 0.5 and 0.6). Elements loaded in a carbon-coated quartz tube and sealed.
Sealed quartz tubes were kept in a box furnace. Heating process in two steps: 120 °C h −1 up to 600 °C, then 60 °C h −1 up to 1100 °C. Mixture held at 1100 °C for 24 h.
Ingots quenched in water.
Ingots taken out of tubes, cleaned using a stainless steel wire brush and subjected to ultrasonication in ethanol for further cleaning. Ingots were dried.

Dried ingot loaded into a 65 ml tall stainless steel jar with two 1/2 inch (12.7 mm) and two 1/4 inch (6.35 mm) hardened stainless steel balls. Vial sealed inside a glove box to prevent oxidation. Ball milled in a SPEX high-energy ball-milling machine (8000 M). Powder loosened inside the glove box after 3 h of ball milling before being milled for a further 4.5 h.
Ball-milled powder loaded in a graphite die (inner diameter 12.7 mm, outer diameter 51 mm, height 38 mm). Hot pressed using a DC hot press to get a sample disk of 4 mm thickness.
After cooling down, the disk was ejected from the graphite die.

Disk cut through the middle to get two disks. One used to make a 2 × 2 × 12 mm^3 bar for electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficient measurements. The other was polished to a uniform thickness for thermal diffusivity measurement. Samples of about 0.6 mm in diameter and 0.7 mm in thickness were also made for specific heat capacity measurements.

processing_method: induction melting of the elements
milling
compaction using current-assisted sintering

processing_steps.notes: Samples with nominal composition Mg2Si0.9875Sb0.0125 were fabricated by induction melting of the elements.

Milling was performed. The difference in particle size is achieved by varying the crushing time of the material and different sieve mesh sizes. MgO has been found in samples crushed in both SiO2 mortars and WC mortars. Ball-milled samples tend to show an inferior performance compared with hand-crushed samples and have a higher MgO content.

Subsequent compaction using current-assisted sintering. It can be deduced that the MgO visible in the XRD is formed during the compaction step. All samples are from the same batch and differ only in their compaction, not in their synthesis parameters.

dopants.site: octahedral positions in the van der Waals' gap

processing_steps.notes: Mixtures of the pure elements (99.5%; Alfa Aesar) of stoichiometry Ti 1+ x S 2 ( x = 0, 0.005, 0.01, 0.015, 0.02, 0.025, 0.05) were heated in sealed fused silica tubes. The resulting powder is composed of plate-like grains of around 1–10 μm (in the ab plane).
This powder was then ground and sieved down to 200 μm to remove large agglomerates.

The Ti 1+ x S 2 powders were placed in tungsten carbide dies of 10 mm diameter and densified by spark plasma sintering (SPS) (FCT HPD 25). The final dimensions of the pellets are around 7 mm in thickness and 10 mm in diameter.
